SHOWHAUS

How much winter sun does a Sydney apartment really get?

SHOWHAUS · from public records, computed 8 Nov 2026 · every figure below comes from the page's own data file

Listings say "light-filled" and "sun-drenched". The honest answer to "will I get sun in June?" depends on the buildings around the block, and that is exactly the part nobody prints. We computed ground sun for ten Sydney addresses in Clovelly, Coogee, Randwick, Bronte and Maroubra, for the day we ran it and for 21 June, the shortest day.

Two answers, eight "unknown"

Sun is only computed when every building within 30 m has a mapped height in OpenStreetMap. Eight of the ten addresses did not meet that bar (unmapped heights or no mapped footprints), so SHOWHAUS shows unknown for them rather than a guess. For the two that did:

AddressGround sun, 8 NovGround sun, 21 June
14 Ethel Street, Randwick11 h 35 of 13 h 308 h 40 of 9 h 45
2/174-178 Brook Street, Coogee9 h 40 of 13 h 305 h 20 of 9 h 45

Median across sample points on the lot. On Brook Street the spread is wide: some points on the lot get no direct sun on 21 June, others about 6 h 20. "Sunny" on that block depends on which side you are on.

What to take from it

  • A spring afternoon tells you little about June. The Brook Street lot loses 4 h 20 of median sun between the two dates, Ethel Street 2 h 55.
  • Ground sun is a lot-level estimate, not a window-level one. It does not know your floor or your balcony.
  • If a tool shows a confident hours figure for every address, ask which buildings it knew the heights of.

Method: NSW cadastre lot outline, OpenStreetMap building footprints and heights (ODbL), NOAA solar position every 10 minutes, flat-ground shadows. Estimated heights are drawn but never counted. Shortcomings are listed on each address page.
